question: How do you turn a layer toward or away from you on the canvas?
context: Mocks: Depth (2.5D) page, section Three ways to turn a layer in 3D. Each canvas there is live: pick the big or small layer and drag. The panel's 3D rows and the depth arrow are the same in all three.

options.label: Arcs on the turn knob
options.summary: Rest the pointer on the knob above a picked layer and two arcs appear on it: drag the flat one sideways to swing the layer, the tall one up or down to tip it. Dragging the knob itself still turns it flat, as today.
pros: Nothing new to find: it grows out of the knob people already use
No mode to enter or leave
Same size on a tiny layer as on a big one
cons: The arcs are small targets close to the knob
Hidden until the pointer rests on the knob
options.mitigation: Generous hit areas on each arc, and the 3D rows in the panel are always there for exact numbers.

options.label: Click the knob, then tip the edges
options.summary: Click the turn knob and the frame switches to 3D: its side handles become tabs. Pull the top tab down and the top comes toward you; push a side tab in and that side swings away. Click the knob again or press Esc to go back.
pros: Feels like holding a card by its edge
Big, easy targets on a large layer
cons: A mode you have to notice you are in
On a small layer the four tabs crowd together
The resize handles are gone while in 3D
options.mitigation: The knob stays filled while in 3D and Esc always leaves it.

options.label: Coloured rings round the pivot
options.summary: A picked layer that can turn in 3D shows Final Cut and Motion's control: a red ring to tip, a green ring to swing, a blue ring to turn flat, centred on the pivot, plus the depth arrow.
pros: What Final Cut Pro and Motion users already know
The most precise of the three
cons: A second turn control beside the knob
On a small layer the rings cover the layer completely
Busy: three rings on every picked layer
options.mitigation: Rings could show only while a key is held, at the cost of being hidden like option A.
